what_its_for: Erdafitinib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a certain type of bladder cancer (urothelial cancer) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It works specifically in patients whose cancer has a change (mutation) in genes called FGFR2 or FGFR3. Your doctor will do a test to check if your cancer has these gene changes before starting this medicine.
how_to_take: Take erdafitinib by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you vomit after taking your dose, do not take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 8 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 9 mg once daily after about 14 to 21 days based on your blood test results (specifically your phosphate levels) and how well you are tolerating the medicine. Your doctor may also lower your dose or temporarily stop the medicine if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions about your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store erdafitinib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of foods that are very high in phosphate (such as dairy products, nuts, beans, and dark colas) especially during the first 3 weeks of treatment, as this can affect your phosphate levels. Avoid St. John's Wort, as it can make erdafitinib less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements, because many drugs can interact with erdafitinib. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen and protective clothing since this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not become pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one month after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: sudden changes in your vision, blurred vision, or eye pain (this could be a serious eye problem called central serous retinopathy or retinal detachment); severe mouth sores or painful sores on your lips or inside your mouth; signs of high phosphate levels such as muscle cramps, joint pain, or itching; severe skin reactions such as blistering, peeling, or a widespread rash; signs of kidney or liver problems such as dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual swelling; or any numbness, tingling, or sores on the palms of your hands or soles of your feet. Also call your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Erdafitinib does not cure cancer, but it works to slow or stop the growth of cancer cells. You may not feel or see immediate changes, but your doctor will check how well the medicine is working through regular imaging tests and check-ups. Some patients begin to see benefits within the first few months of treatment. It is important to keep taking the medicine as directed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Male patients with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Older adults: This medicine can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects, so your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Eye problems: Tell your doctor about any existing eye conditions before starting treatment, as regular eye exams will be needed during therapy.
